newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Skala plans to boost its stake in Centrum.
newsitem.headline: Skala plans to boost its stake in Centrum.

text.p: Hungarian holding firm Skala-Coop Rt has offered to subscribe a one billion forint share package, to be issued by retail chain Centrum Aruhazak Rt, Hungarian news agency MTI said.

"Skala-Coop Rt, jointly with Kereskedelmi es Hitelbank Rt (K&H Bank), has made an offer to raise Centrum's five billion forints issued share capital by one billion," Skala's President and CEO, Istvan Imre was quoted as saying.

The share issue would bring Centrum's share capital to six billion, while would allow an additional 16 percent stake to Skala in Centrum, it said, adding that Skala's stake would still remain below 50 percent.
The one-billion-forint capital increase would be fully subscribed by Skala, MTI said.
It was not immediately clear what K&H Bank's role would be in the transaction.
The Budapest Stock Exchange suspended trading in Skala shares after a too rapid intraday rise of over 20 percent.
